I just wanted to weigh in on the neck trim. My go to guide of reference is: Exactly where the neck ends and the the "jaw fold" begins. Let me elaborate...If you run the tip of your index finger along the front of your neck, exactly upwards, with your head facing straight, and it stops (without changing direction of your finger), this is where I trim up to. From my own experience, doing this with your trimmer, gives the look, shape, and feel of a full beard after a few months time. It's basically (for me) as simple as running the trimmer up the neck until it stops, and moving to the next part of the neck, until you've shaped out that "jaw fold," I so ineloquently described. To go even more in-depth, the "jaw fold" is basically where the soft under-palate of your lower jaw meets your neck. Using this principal has cut down my personal trimming time immensely, while at the same time, has kept my beard looking full, and well kept near the neck.

I have to say, this method may not be for everyone, but it's saved me a LOT of time and energy.

I hope it helped someone!

Edit: After finishing the line on the "jaw fold", use your hands and pull off the loose beard hair where you were trimming. After removing the loose beard hair, carefully take your trimmers along that same line...follow the line with your trimmers. Hold the trimmers at an angle away from your lower jaw and neck, to avoid cutting more hair than you intended. Doing this will help create a blend-effect at the area you just trimmed (the neck line) and, if done right, will give the appearance of a natural, blended line - from neck, to beard.
